docs.root.component: A root is a node that nobody placed. It has no owner, and no size of its own — its extent
comes from what it holds.
There is no separate storage object in the kit: every node hangs off a root, so the root is
the store. Nothing sits above roots, which is why there is no word for the thing that holds
them.
```ts
import { node, add, byId } from "game-kit"
const root = node("root")
add(root, node("hand"))   // a child; the root is still the one node nobody placed
byId(root, "hand")        // an index derived from the tree, not a second store
## One name per tree
Adding a second `hand` throws, and so does adding a subtree that carries a taken name anywhere
inside it. Replacing the older node would be worse than the error: the picture would still
look right while the identity behind it was lost. Two separate trees may each hold a `hand` —
names only have to be unique within one tree.
## Notes
- Being a root is not a type or a flag; it is the absence of an owner. Detach a child and it
becomes a root on the spot. A root cannot become someone's child — it would stop being one.
- There are two roots on screen, and one difference between them: the camera transforms the
canvas root and leaves the HUD root alone. That is the whole anchoring rule — there is no
`anchor` field, the root a node belongs to is the answer.
- Pixels live in the host. Nodes are measured in units; the host owns the view, its size and
the resize observer, and works out the HUD etalon as a fraction of the viewport.

The names come from the spec rather than a generator, which is what lets two devices agree on
which node a move is about. Type them in the controls and the tree follows.
No `Container` atom is involved. Parent and child are part of a node: a place in the tree has
two directions, and one without the other means nothing. `Container` adds how children are
arranged, not whether they can exist.
docs.root.alone: The same node as `Node → Bare`, seen from the other side: nobody placed it, so it is a root.
